## 14.1 Study 1: Adults with Acromegaly Naïve or Previously Treated on a Somatostatin Analog
CRN00808-08 (Trial 08)	Adults with nonpharmacologically treated acromegaly	Control type: Placebo concurrent
Study 1 (NCT05192382) enrolled 111 adult participants with biochemically uncontrolled acromegaly.
The safety of PALSONIFY was evaluated in adults with acromegaly in two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 studies.

The safety of PALSONIFY was evaluated in adults with acromegaly in two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 studies. Study 1 was a 24-week, randomized, placebo-controlled study in 111 adults who were naive or previously treated on a somatostatin analog and biochemically uncontrolled at randomization.

population.text: Adults with biochemically uncontrolled acromegaly, treatment naïve or previously treated on a somatostatin analog and washed out

citations.quote: Study 1 (NCT05192382) enrolled 111 adult participants with biochemically uncontrolled acromegaly.

endpoint.text: Proportion of participants achieving biochemical control (IGF-1 level ≤ 1.0 × ULN) at Week 24 versus placebo

citations.quote: The primary endpoint was the proportion of PALSONIFY participants achieving biochemical control (defined as IGF-1 level \le 1.0 \times \text{ULN}) compared to placebo-treated participants.
Participants were randomized to receive either PALSONIFY (n=54) or placebo (n=57) for the 24-week treatment period.

result.text: At Week 24, 56% of PALSONIFY participants achieved biochemical control vs 5% of placebo (p < 0.0001)

citations.quote: At Week 24, 56% of PALSONIFY participants achieved biochemical control compared to 5% of placebo-treated participants (p-value < 0.0001) (Table 5).
## 14.2 Study 2: Adults with Acromegaly Previously Controlled on a Somatostatin Analog
CRN00808-09 (Trial 09)	Adults with acromegaly who were switched from monotherapy with octreotide or lanreotide	Control type: Placebo concurrent
Study 2 (NCT04837040) enrolled 58 participants who were previously biochemically controlled
The safety of PALSONIFY was evaluated in adults with acromegaly in two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 studies.
Participants were randomized to receive either PALSONIFY (n=30) or placebo (n=28) for the 36-week treatment period.
The effectiveness of PALSONIFY for treatment of adults with acromegaly was evaluated in two randomized, double-blind, parallel group, placebo-controlled clinical studies.

population.text: Adults with acromegaly previously biochemically controlled on injectable depot octreotide or lanreotide

citations.quote: Study 2 (NCT04837040) enrolled 58 participants who were previously biochemically controlled (defined as IGF-1 levels \le 1.0 \times \text{ULN} during screening and at randomization) on injectable depot octreotide or lanreotide somatostatin analog formulations.

endpoint.text: Proportion of participants with biochemical response (IGF-1 ≤ 1.0 × ULN) at Week 36 versus placebo

citations.quote: The primary endpoint was the proportion of PALSONIFY participants with biochemical response (i.e., IGF-1 \le 1.0 \times \text{ULN}) compared to placebo-treated participants.
Participants were randomized to receive either PALSONIFY (n=30) or placebo (n=28) for the 36-week treatment period.

result.text: At Week 36, 83% of PALSONIFY participants maintained biochemical control vs 4% of placebo (p < 0.0001)

citations.quote: At Week 36, 83% of PALSONIFY participants maintained biochemical control compared to 4% of placebo-treated participants (p-value < 0.0001) (Table 7).

indication.text: Treatment of adults with acromegaly who had an inadequate response to surgery and/or for whom surgery is not an option

citations.quote: PALSONIFY is indicated for the treatment of adults with acromegaly who had an inadequate response to surgery and/or for whom surgery is not an option.

target_moa.text: Selective somatostatin receptor 2 (SSTR2) agonist that suppresses GH and IGF-1 secretion

citations.quote: Similar to the natural hormone somatostatin, paltusotine suppresses growth hormone (GH) and insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) secretion.
Paltusotine exerts its pharmacological activity via selective agonism (>4000-fold) at somatostatin receptor 2 (SSTR2) and exhibits little or no affinity for other SST receptor subtypes.
PALSONIFY tablets contain paltusotine hydrochloride, a somatostatin receptor agonist.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (≥5%): diarrhea, abdominal pain, nausea, decreased appetite, sinus bradycardia, hyperglycemia, palpitations, and gastroenteritis; cholelithiasis and complications reported in 6% of participants

citations.quote: Most common adverse reactions (\ge 5\%) are diarrhea, abdominal pain, nausea, decreased appetite, sinus bradycardia, hyperglycemia, palpitations, and gastroenteritis (6.1).
Cholelithiasis and its complications were reported in 10/173 (6%) participants during Studies 1 and 2

vote.text: No advisory committee meeting was held

citations.quote: No meeting of an advisory committee was held because the application did not raise significant safety, efficacy or other issues requiring input from external experts.

detail.text: NDA 219070 received September 25, 2024 and approved for use as recommended in the agreed-upon labeling

citations.quote: Please refer to your new drug application (NDA) received September 25, 2024, and your amendments, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for Palsonify (paltusotine) tablets.
It is approved, effective on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon labeling.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan Drug designation for the treatment of acromegaly, granted July 7, 2020

citations.quote: Paltusotine was granted *Orphan Drug* designation for the treatment of acromegaly by the Office of Orphan Products Development on July 7, 2020 (#DRU-2017-5766).

summary.text: Standard review NDA supported by two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials; paltusotine held Orphan Drug designation for acromegaly.

citations.quote: Priority or standard	Standard
This NDA includes data from two randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trials to provide substantial evidence of the safety and efficacy of paltusotine in patients with acromegaly.
Paltusotine was granted *Orphan Drug* designation for the treatment of acromegaly by the Office of Orphan Products Development on July 7, 2020 (#DRU-2017-5766).
